58/S0.subgoal: Describe the stages of the 3D graphics pipeline, from object representation to scan conversion.

58/S1.subgoal: Explain the fundamental problem of rasterization: mapping continuous device coordinates to discrete pixel grids.

58/S2.subgoal: Compare methods for rendering points and lines, focusing on efficient, integer-based algorithms like Bresenham's.

58/S3.subgoal: Explain the importance of avoiding floating-point operations and define the problems of aliasing and anti-aliasing.

58/S4.subgoal: Analyze the increased computational complexity required to render realistic and dynamic scenes in virtual reality.

58/S5.subgoal: Describe how programmers utilize APIs and graphics libraries to abstract and implement the graphics pipeline.

58/S6.subgoal: Outline and describe the layered architecture of a complete virtual reality system.

58/S7.subgoal: Explain the need for parallelism in graphics operations and the role of the dedicated Graphics Processing Unit (GPU).

58/S8.subgoal: Describe the internal architecture of a GPU and how it processes the rendering pipeline using parallel data streams.

58/S9.subgoal: Detail how GPUs handle specialized tasks like surface texturing and hidden surface removal using the depth buffer.

58/S10.subgoal: Summarize the methods used by software libraries and GPUs to manage and reduce the computational complexity of VR rendering.
